description: Single-DGX-Spark Qwen3.8 Flash Next on Ash Hart's TensorFold engine v0.6.6 (exact decoding, custom CUDA kernels JIT-compiled on first start, stock upstream source) with turboderp's EXL3 3.05 bits-per-weight pack (branch 3.05bpw_h5_ng5; 85 GB including a 32.6 GB n-gram table that stays memory-mapped from the checkpoint; MTP layer included). TensorFold marks its EXL3 path experimental and runs it on one GPU only (upstream refuses --tp 2 and --ple-on-ssd on EXL3 packs); the platform harness has no distributed support anyway. Serves one request at a time by default (upstream CUDA default; the concurrency setting enables shared rounds) at the 262,144-token window with a bf16 KV cache. Text only here: TensorFold adds Flash Next image input on CUDA from 0.6.1 (video from 0.6.3, which needs PyAV, not installed), and this recipe does not expose it. Upstream measured on one DGX Spark: 81 tok/s code sampled and 59 tok/s chat sampled (MLX 4-bit checkpoint: 77 and 63), prefill at about 0.4x the MLX checkpoint, 52 GB of GPU memory for the weights and 57.6 GiB allocated after loading at 262,144 tokens (upstream claims, unmeasured here); the memory envelope below adds the mapped n-gram table to that figure. Only the 3.05bpw_h5_ng5 branch is measured upstream. The model weights are under the Qwen Community License 1.0 (attribution above 100M MAU or US$20M monthly revenue; separate licence for Model-as-a-Service or AI Work Assistant businesses); TensorFold is Apache-2.0 from 0.6.0 (MIT up to 0.5.0). TensorFold v0.6.6 at cb2ebf0540f42604e2759b2ddef497861e928248, the newest release of TensorFold's Python engine line (0.6; TensorFold 1.x is a native binary that serves only Nemotron on CUDA), keeps every option this recipe passes. Per upstream's release notes it runs CUDA prompts at bf16 by default and serves Prometheus /metrics, fills prompts inside the decode rounds when concurrency is above 1, resumes resends on Flash Next, and reads consolidated EXL3 n-gram tables; the existing context bound, KV/drafting defaults, and one-stream resource profile are retained. From 0.6.1 to 0.6.6 upstream's release notes add, among others, the Anthropic Messages API (/v1/messages), optional API keys (not set here), /v1/decisions scoring and joint prefill of prompts that wait together when concurrency is above 1. 0.6.4 refuses GPUs below sm_120 at startup (the Spark's GB10 is sm_121). The pinned ARM64 image includes xgrammar 0.2.8 and Apache TVM FFI 0.1.11 for OpenAI response_format structured-output requests. Thinking is chosen per request (chat template kwargs or sampling parameters), not as a recipe option; server default: Open a think block by default (upstream default: --thinking).
title: Qwen3.8 Flash Next EXL3 3.05bpw TensorFold single Spark
